bug_semantics: Ech0 installed internal/i18n.Middleware() on the global Gin router, so every unauthenticated request supplied its raw, trimmed Accept-Language header to NewLocalizer. NewLocalizer passed that unbounded value directly to go-i18n, whose tag parsing reaches golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage. The x/text CVE-2022-32149 guard counts '-' separators but the scanner also aliases '_' to '-', so a near-1 MiB header made from malformed underscore-separated subtags bypasses the guard and exercises quadratic gobble/memmove behavior. The same unbounded parser was also reachable through X-Locale and the lang query parameter via ResolveLocale, with those explicit-locale paths potentially adding another parse. This is an unauthenticated CPU denial of service on public routes.
flaw_origin: Application-boundary flaw first created by b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516: that single ordinary commit added the i18n implementation, directly forwarded acceptLanguage to goi18n.NewLocalizer, read Accept-Language from the request without a size/shape bound, and globally registered the middleware. The underlying parser behavior pre-existed in dependencies, but Ech0's remotely reachable unbounded data path did not exist in the immediate parent.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-mqxv-9rm6-w8qc documents the request path Middleware -> ctx.GetHeader("Accept-Language") -> setLocaleContext -> NewLocalizer -> language.ParseAcceptLanguage, the '_' alias bypass, approximately 1.5 seconds CPU for a 1 MiB hostile header (and approximately 7.9 seconds with X-Locale), unauthenticated reachability, affected <=4.8.2, patched 5.0.1+, and fix PR https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0-ghsa-mqxv-9rm6-w8qc/pull/1.

Run `git show --format=fuller --stat --patch b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go go.mod go.sum` in the validated clone. The commit creates internal/i18n/i18n.go; ResolveLocale passes joined raw values to language.ParseAcceptLanguage, NewLocalizer returns goi18n.NewLocalizer(bundle, locale, acceptLanguage), Middleware reads strings.TrimSpace(ctx.GetHeader("Accept-Language")), and internal/router/middleware.go adds r.Use(i18nUtil.Middleware()). It also first adds go-i18n v2.6.1 to go.mod.

The independent history cross-checks converge on the same BIC. `git log -L ':Middleware:internal/i18n/i18n.go' main` reaches the /dev/null addition in b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516; `git log -L ':NewLocalizer:internal/i18n/i18n.go' main` shows the unfiltered sink added by that commit and changed only by the fix. Pickaxe commands `git log --all -S'ctx.GetHeader("Accept-Language")' -- internal/i18n/i18n.go`, `git log --all -S'return goi18n.NewLocalizer(bundle, locale, acceptLanguage)' -- internal/i18n/i18n.go`, and `git log --all -S'r.Use(i18nUtil.Middleware())' -- internal/router/middleware.go` all identify b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 as the first addition on the application history; later dc03197eeb4b5f28ebe794f45732cd4d04d53b1c refactors the middleware but preserves the unbounded sink.

Direct parent verification: `git ls-tree -r --name-only b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go go.mod` lists only go.mod and internal/router/middleware.go, not internal/i18n/i18n.go. `git show b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6:internal/router/middleware.go` contains Recovery, Cors, and WriteGuard only, with no i18n registration; searching that parent's go.mod for go-i18n produces no match. Thus the immediate parent lacks both the vulnerable parser path and its global exposure.

`git cat-file -p b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516` gives exactly one parent, b00c0f7da80cdbf4f4bd84a0c557ae03c88775a6, and a direct tree diff. It is not a merge, release, move, revert, or publicly decomposable squash aggregate, so the ordinary commit itself is the smallest public-history BIC and decomposed_shas is empty.

Introduction boundary: `git show -s --format='%H %ad %s' v4.0.0^{}` resolves v4.0.0 to 93b935c5b64020c7475abb9df071fdf8663b9f84, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only v4.0.0 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go` has no output. v4.1.0 resolves to d1f0768e8d469179d5ee8634c2c3311ed31e1d26; `git grep -n -E 'Accept-Language|NewLocalizer\(bundle|i18nUtil.Middleware' v4.1.0 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/router/middleware.go` shows the raw header, unfiltered NewLocalizer sink, and global middleware registration. Therefore v4.1.0 is the first tagged affected release in this Git history.

Closing fix: `git show --format=fuller --patch a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go internal/i18n/i18n_test.go` shows commit a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 adding maxAcceptLanguageSeparators=32 and sanitizeAcceptLanguage, applying it to every ResolveLocale part and immediately before goi18n.NewLocalizer. This directly closes the Accept-Language, X-Locale, lang-query, and later-caller sinks; its sole parent is ccfb304534d8f1260611bb4af3d3f3ab69ac00ed.

Fix release boundary: v5.0.0 resolves to 4deb936608843fab40692788cf299700bb6637bf and `git grep -n -E 'Accept-Language|sanitizeAcceptLanguage|NewLocalizer\(bundle' v5.0.0 -- internal/i18n/i18n.go` shows the raw header and unfiltered goi18n.NewLocalizer call with no sanitizer. `git tag --contains a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 --sort=version:refname` first lists v5.0.2/ech0-5.0.2 among normal version tags; v5.0.2 resolves to release commit f715214732db93067718150cb3b2bad8fe9be827, and the same grep at v5.0.2 shows sanitizer calls. The validated clone has no v5.0.1 tag, so v5.0.2 is the first repository-verifiable fixed tag even though the first-party advisory declares 5.0.1+ patched.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516` shows human author and committer `L1nSn0w <l1nsn0w@qq.com>` and the message `feat: Integrate internationalization support across the application` with bullet points, but no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI tool trailer, bot identity, or other explicit AI marker. The later fix object's `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>` is AI-only-on-fix and is excluded by the BIC-only rule.
reasoning: The vulnerable capability is not merely the presence of a parser dependency: it is the complete remotely reachable chain that supplies an attacker-controlled, essentially net/http-sized header to the quadratic parser on every route. b55edabd228d3de41e781bd3100f2e1ee0835516 is the smallest public commit containing that complete chain because it simultaneously creates the unfiltered parser wrappers and installs their middleware globally, while direct inspection proves the parent lacks them. Later i18n changes preserve rather than originate the flaw. a5e77c4af60ead1cad3b3e8e0a3ed6f30892ed09 is both the direct code fix and the closing fix because it bounds separators at the two true sinks, and tagged-tree comparison proves the vulnerable/fixed transition. The BIC commit object has no explicit AI evidence and is authored/committed by a non-bot human identity. Protocol requires ignoring the explicit Claude trailer on the later fix, so the only supported verdict is NOT_AI.
